paper.title_en: Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian
paper.abstract_en: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.
